title: Universal-homeomorphism invariance
statement:
If $u:X'\to X$ is a universal homeomorphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], then the morphisms of small etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] induced by $u$ give an equivalence of small etale
topoi, i.e. an equivalence of the categories of etale sheaves

$$
 \operatorname{Sh}(X_{\Et})\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Sh}(X'_{\Et}),
$$

compatible with the inverse and direct image functors and with cohomology.
The equivalence preserves and reflects covering families and is compatible
with identities, composition, and pullback of sheaves and cohomology.

proof.text: (Equivalence of sites, coverings.) Let $u:X'\to X$ be a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. By [lemma-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence] (Stacks Tag 04DZ, the theorem on topological invariance of the small etale site) the base-change functor $u^{\Et}:X_{\Et}\to X'_{\Et}$, $V\mapsto V\times_XX'$, of the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] is an equivalence of the underlying categories. By [lemma-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-coverings] a family $\{V_i\to V\}$ of etale $X$-schemes is jointly surjective, i.e. a covering of $X_{\Et}$, if and only if its base change $\{V_i\times_XX'\to V\times_XX'\}$ is a covering of $X'_{\Et}$. This is the clause that the equivalence preserves and reflects covering families; together the two give part (1) of Stacks Tag 03SI, an isomorphism of sites $X_{\Et}\simeq X'_{\Et}$ (the step that Stacks omits, that coverings correspond, is the second cited lemma).

source.place: Tag 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance), proof, first two sentences; Tag 04DZ (theorem-topological-invariance)

proof.text: (Equivalence of topoi; inverse and direct image.) By [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos] (Stacks Tag 03SI (2)), the inverse image $u^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\Et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is an equivalence of the categories of etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. The direct image $u_*$, $(u_*F)(V)=F(V\times_XX')$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], is right adjoint to $u^{-1}$ with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. A right adjoint of an equivalence is a quasi-inverse of it, and the unit and counit of the adjunction are then isomorphisms (if $u^{-1}$ has a quasi-inverse $Q$, then $Q$ is also right adjoint to $u^{-1}$, so $Q\cong u_*$ by uniqueness of adjoints, compatibly with the units). Hence $u_*$ is an equivalence quasi-inverse to $u^{-1}$, $\eta_u:\mathrm{id}\to u_*u^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon_u:u^{-1}u_*\to\mathrm{id}$ are isomorphisms, and both functors are exact. This is the equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\Et})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(X'_{\Et})$ of the statement and its compatibility with inverse and direct images.

source.place: Tag 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance), part (2), proof: 'Parts (2) and (3) follow formally from (1)'

proof.text: (Cohomology.) For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ and $q\ge0$, let $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\to H^q(X'_{\Et},u^{-1}F)$ be the pullback map on etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. By [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos] (Stacks Tag 03SI (3)) it is an isomorphism for every $F$ and every $q$. (Its argument: $u^{-1}$ is an exact equivalence, so it carries an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ to an injective resolution $u^{-1}F\to u^{-1}I^\bullet$, and on global sections $u^*$ is $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\eta_u}\Gamma(X,u_*u^{-1}I^\bullet)=\Gamma(X',u^{-1}I^\bullet)$, an isomorphism of complexes since $\eta_u$ is one by step 2.) This is the compatibility of the equivalence with cohomology.

(Identities and composition.) For $u=\mathrm{id}_X$ the base-change functor is isomorphic to the identity of $X_{\Et}$ via $V\times_XX\cong V$, and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (3) gives $e_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ and $d_X:(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$. For universal homeomorphisms $u:X'\to X$ and $v:X''\to X'$, the composite $u\circ v$ is a universal homeomorphism (the base change of $u\circ v$ along any $T\to X$ is the composite of the base change of $u$ along $T\to X$ and of $v$ along $T\times_XX'\to X'$, a composite of homeomorphisms; [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]); the base-change functor of $u\circ v$ is isomorphic to the composite of those of $u$ and $v$ by $(V\times_XX')\times_{X'}X''\cong V\times_XX''$, and on sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (1),(2) give the isomorphisms $d_{u,v}:(u\circ v)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}u_*v_*$ and $c_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$, compatible with the units. So the equivalence of step 2 for a composite is the composite of the equivalences, and that for an identity is the identity, up to these canonical isomorphisms. On cohomology, [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (4) gives $(u\circ v)^*=H^q(c_{u,v,F})\circ v^*\circ u^*$ and $H^q(e_{X,F})\circ\mathrm{id}_X^*=\mathrm{id}$, so the isomorphisms of step 3 are compatible with identities and composition.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence ('naturally in the schemes and compatible with identities and composites') and last sentence ('the equivalence of a composite is the composite of the equivalences')

proof.text: (Pullback.) Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes, $Y'=Y\times_XX'$, $u':Y'\to Y$ and $g':Y'\to X'$ the projections, so $u\circ g'=g\circ u'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-base-change] $u'$ is a universal homeomorphism, so steps 2 and 3 apply to $u'$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) to the two factorizations of $w=u\circ g'=g\circ u'$ gives $c_{g,u'}^{-1}\circ c_{u,g'}:g'^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}w^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}u'^{-1}g^{-1}$, the commutative square of inverse images: the equivalences $u^{-1}$ and $u'^{-1}$ commute with pullback of sheaves along $g$ and $g'$. For the quasi-inverses: using the isomorphisms $\eta_u$, $\varepsilon_{u'}$ of step 2, $u'_*g'^{-1}\cong u'_*g'^{-1}u^{-1}u_*\cong u'_*u'^{-1}g^{-1}u_*\cong g^{-1}u_*$. On cohomology, [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (4) applied to both factorizations of $w$ gives, for an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$, $H^q(c_{u,g',F})\circ g'^*\circ u^*=w^*=H^q(c_{g,u',F})\circ u'^*\circ g^*$, i.e. the isomorphisms $u^*$ (on $X$) and $u'^*$ (on $Y$) of step 3 commute with the pullback maps $g^*$ and $g'^*$, up to the canonical isomorphism $c_{g,u'}^{-1}c_{u,g'}$. This is the compatibility with pullback of sheaves and cohomology.

source.place: ## Proof, last sentence ('for a base change u' of u ... the equivalences of u and u' form a commutative square with the inverse-image functors')
